title: Wetlands Conservation and Access Improvement Act of 2025
official_summary:
Wetlands Conservation and Access Improvement Act of 2025

This act extends until FY2033 a requirement for the interest earned on certain funds held in the Federal Aid to Wildlife Restoration Fund to be distributed to states for carrying out certain wildlife conservation and restoration programs. Specifically, the act extends the period in which the interest earned on revenue generated from excise taxes on certain firearms, ammunition, and archery equipment must be used for wildlife conservation and restoration programs established under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act. This requirement was set to expire at the beginning of FY2026. In the absence of this requirement, this funding would be distributed to states, according to a formula, for (1) wildlife restoration, (2) hunter education and safety, (3) multistate conservation grants, and (4) administrative costs.

summary.headline: Law keeps interest from federal taxes on guns, ammunition, and archery gear going to wetlands conservation programs through fiscal year 2033.
summary.what_it_does: Federal excise taxes on certain firearms, ammunition, and archery equipment go into a wildlife fund, and that money earns interest. This law extends a rule that sends the interest to wildlife conservation and restoration programs set up under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act. The rule was set to end at the start of fiscal year 2026 and now runs through fiscal year 2033. Without the extension, the interest would have gone to states by formula for wildlife restoration, hunter education and safety, multistate conservation grants, and administrative costs.

who_it_affects.group: Groups and projects funded under the North American Wetlands Conservation Act
who_it_affects.how: They continue to receive the interest earned on the wildlife fund through fiscal year 2033.
They will not receive this interest money through the state formula for wildlife restoration, hunter education, and related uses while the extension is in place.

who_it_affects.group: People who buy firearms, ammunition, or archery equipment
who_it_affects.how: The law does not change the taxes they pay, only where the interest earned on that tax money goes.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted November 25, 2025; the extension covers fiscal years 2026 through 2033.
